operational_costs.transport: Phase 2 C routes stdio (pl-worker, bounded validated frames over pipes), shm (memfd regions, validated control frames) and inproc (libpl_inproc.so in the interpreter, least safe); each row keeps its route label
operational_costs.deployment_artifacts: pl-kernel, pl-worker and libpl_inproc.so built by the project check with the pinned toolchain, plus the Python codec; none ships by default
operational_costs.observability: bench evidence only (per-row cgroup CPU, group peak, route label, raw blocks); no production telemetry exists for the C path
operational_costs.failure_handling: a C failure, refusal or call deadline fails or blocks the row in evidence; a production fallback to Python is not designed yet
operational_costs.retries_idempotency: a request is a pure computation over its input, so a repeat is idempotent; the bench never retries a failed call
operational_costs.ownership_abi: the example project owns the worker protocol and the in-process ABI; a production owner is not assigned (owner)
operational_costs.native_boundary_maintenance: the 23 project gates, sanitizers and fuzz replay on each change; the C models must track the Python reference, the oracle and the locked tolerances
